title: Count Trailing Zeros in Factorial
description:
Return the number of trailing zeros in `n!` (n factorial). Trailing zeros come from factors of 10 = 2 × 5. Since there are always more 2s than 5s in a factorial, count the factors of 5.

**Example:**
```
trailing_zeros(5) → 1   # 5! = 120
trailing_zeros(10) → 2  # 10! = 3628800
trailing_zeros(25) → 6  # 25! = ...000000
```
hint: Count multiples of 5, 25, 125, ... in n. Use: count = 0; while n >= 5: n //= 5; count += n.
